requirements.statement: As a Customer, I want to register my personal details (name, address, phone), so that the system can uniquely identify me.

acceptance_criteria.text: All of name, address and phone must be provided and non‑empty.
The system assigns a unique identifier to each customer record.
Given a registration request, when the data passes validation, then the system stores the customer and returns a success response.

requirements.statement: As a Customer, I want to optionally add a bank account, so that I can use it as a payment method.

acceptance_criteria.text: A bank account may be associated with a customer at most once.
Given a customer who has no bank account, when the customer adds a bank account, then the system stores the account and links it to the customer.
The bank‑account field is optional; the customer record remains valid without it.

requirements.statement: As a Customer, I want to view product information (name, description, price, image), so that I can decide what to buy.

acceptance_criteria.text: Each product must have name, description, price and image URL; all are mandatory.
Product price is stored as a decimal number.
Given a request to view the catalog, when the request is authenticated, then the system returns the list of products with the required attributes.

requirements.statement: As a Customer, I want to submit an order that contains one or more order items, each referencing an existing product and a payment method, so that I can purchase the items.

acceptance_criteria.text: Given a known customer, when the customer submits an order with at least one order item referencing existing products and a valid payment method, then the system creates an order with status submitted, order date = submission date, and total amount = Σ(quantity × unitPrice).
Given an unknown customer, when the customer attempts to submit an order, then the system rejects the submission and no order is recorded.
An order must contain at least one order item; otherwise the submission is rejected.
All referenced products must exist; otherwise the submission is rejected.

requirements.statement: As OrderStaff, I want to receive a submitted order and set its status to pending, so that the order enters the processing workflow.

acceptance_criteria.text: Given an order with status submitted, when OrderStaff receives the order, then the system changes the status to pending.
The status transition submitted → pending is allowed; any other transition is rejected.
The order’s status cannot be changed after it reaches closed.

requirements.statement: As OrderStaff, I want to mark a pending order as filled, so that it is ready for shipping.

acceptance_criteria.text: Given a pending order, when OrderStaff marks it as filled, then the system changes the status to filled.
The status transition pending → filled is allowed; any other transition is rejected.
When an order becomes filled, its order items remain attached (composition).

requirements.statement: As OrderStaff, I want to ship a filled order, so that it is dispatched to the customer.

acceptance_criteria.text: Given a filled order, when OrderStaff ships the order, then the system changes the status to shipped.
The status transition filled → shipped is allowed; any other transition is rejected.
Shipping does not alter the status of any associated invoice or payment.

requirements.statement: As OrderStaff, I want to decline a pending order, so that it is closed without further processing.

acceptance_criteria.text: Given a pending order, when OrderStaff declines it, then the system changes the status to closed.
The status transition pending → closed is allowed; any other transition is rejected.
A declined order cannot later have an invoice raised.

requirements.statement: As OrderStaff, I want to close a shipped order whose invoice is paid, so that the transaction is completed.

acceptance_criteria.text: Given a shipped order whose linked invoice has status paid, when OrderStaff closes the order, then the system changes the order status to closed.
The system rejects an attempt to close a shipped order whose invoice is not paid.
Once an order is closed its status cannot be changed further.

requirements.statement: As an Accountant, I want to raise an invoice for a filled or shipped order that has no invoice, so that the customer can be billed.

acceptance_criteria.text: Given a filled (or shipped) order with no invoice, when Accountant raises an invoice with date, amount, payment method and status issued, then the system creates the invoice linked to the order.
An order can have at most one invoice; a second attempt is rejected.
Invoices can be raised only when the order status is filled or shipped.

requirements.statement: As a Customer, I want to submit a payment against an issued invoice, so that the invoice can be settled.

acceptance_criteria.text: Given an issued invoice, when a Customer submits a payment with date, amount and payment method, then the system creates a payment with status pending linked to the invoice.
Payments cannot be submitted against an invoice whose status is paid.
The system permits multiple payments per invoice; each payment is recorded separately.

requirements.statement: As an Accountant, I want to confirm a pending payment, so that the related invoice becomes paid.

acceptance_criteria.text: Given a pending payment, when Accountant confirms it, then the system changes the payment status to completed and sets the linked invoice status to paid.
The status transition pending → completed is allowed; any other transition is rejected.
Confirming a payment does not alter the status of the associated order.

requirements.statement: As an Accountant, I want to reject a pending payment, so that the failure is recorded and the invoice remains unchanged.

acceptance_criteria.text: Given a pending payment, when Accountant rejects it, then the system changes the payment status to failed and leaves the invoice and order statuses unchanged.
The status transition pending → failed is allowed; any other transition is rejected.
After a payment is failed, further payments may be submitted (see US‑11).

requirements.statement: The system shall register an order containing up to 50 order items and respond within 2 seconds for at least 95% of submissions.
The system shall support at least 200 concurrent users and process at least 20 order submissions per second while meeting the response time of NFR-01.
The system shall authenticate every user before granting access to any customer, order, invoice or payment data and shall reject 100% of unauthenticated requests.
The system shall allow only users holding the accountant role to confirm or reject a payment and shall reject the same request from any other user.
The system shall protect customer personal data and bank account numbers by encrypting them in transit with TLS 1.2 or higher and at rest.
The system shall be available for at least 99.5% of each calendar month, excluding scheduled maintenance announced at least 24 hours in advance.
When a server failure occurs, the system shall resume accepting requests within 15 minutes without losing any order, invoice or payment recorded before the failure.
